agents.name: Claude Code
agents.quote: These days, given a slow-loading website, even as someone who’s written about browser performance for years and who literally worked on a browser performance team, I would probably just chuck a Chrome trace at Claude Code and have it suggest improvements. In fact I’ve done this very thing in my day job and gotten some good results.

review_style.quote: Run a Claude sub-agent, Codex, and Cursor Bugbot to find bugs in this PR ranked by critical/high/medium/low. Once they’re all done, review their findings, do your own research to rule out false positives, and write a final report.

also.quote: Have an agent fix all the criticals and highs (with my guidance on the proper solution), then repeat until no criticals/highs
For example, I find myself spending a lot of time these days in code review, using tools like my triple-agent code review skill as well as Geoffrey Litt’s explain-diff skill.

signature.caption: three-agent PR bug hunt
signature.why: Our pick: Claude, Codex and Cursor Bugbot each review the PR, then the main agent cross-checks their findings to drop hallucinated bugs.
signature.quote: In my experience, this skill always finds tons of bugs in a PR, and the false positive rate is near zero.

archetype.why: He uses agents to make code better, not faster: multi-agent review on every PR, and no AI in his writing.

signature_quote.value: And you can use them just as effectively to write high-quality code more slowly.
